prompt:
Executive Summary
Create a Roblox Demonfall-inspired open-world action RPG set in a Taishō-era fantasy. The player starts as a human in a rural earth-biome village, returns home to find their family slain by a demon, then splinters into two paths: Survive = become a Slayer, Die = become a Demon. A cinematic prologue and mobile-friendly obby tutorial teach basic movement (run, jump, camera), combat (light/heavy attack, block, dash), and UI (controls overlay before drawing the katana). Players choose a family (clan) with unique buffs and cosmetic style during character creation (e.g. Kanroji clan gives +15% damage, Kamado clan +20% EXP and Sun-immunity). The core gameplay loop emphasizes dynamic combat with stamina/breathing management, deep progression (skill tree, breathing styles, Blood Demon Arts), cooperative PvE missions (with scalable difficulty), and a day/night cycle that makes nights dangerous (demons hunt; they die in daylight without Sun immunity).

Key Systems:

Combat: Simple mobile controls (touch buttons) and PC controls (keyboard/mouse) for light/heavy slash, block, dash/sprint, weapon draw/sheath, plus a visible Stamina/Breath meter. Advanced skills are unlocked via breathing styles (9-12 styles) or demon arts.
Progression: Players earn skill points by killing demons, completing quests, and conquering missions. A branching skill tree lets them improve stats (Strength, Endurance, Speed, Steel-Lungs to slow breathing drain, Dash upgrades, etc.) and unlock special moves.
Breathing Styles (Slayer paths): At least ten breathing arts (Water, Flame, Thunder, Wind, Mist, Stone, Love, Serpent, Sound, Beast, plus secret Sun/Moon) exist, each with trainer NPCs and unlock quests. Four beginner-friendly styles (Water, Flame, Thunder, Beast) are accessible early; higher-tier styles require harder quests or demos. For example, Beast Breathing (dual-wield style) requires Level 10, 10,000 Yen, dual katanas and a hidden mountain cave trainer. Clan synergy is important: e.g., Hashibira clan grants +10% damage for Beast users.
Demon Path: If a player dies in the prologue, they become a demon with regeneration, Blood Arts, and increased power. Demons climb their own boss ladder (ordinary demons → Demon Ranks → Lower Moon bosses → Upper Moon bosses). Slayer players may choose to become demons by consuming Muzan's blood (a rare item or boss drop) and waiting in "hybrid" limbo (taking real-time hours based on level). Conversely, demons can revert via a rare Wipe Potion sold by a special merchant, or by codes, reflecting community lore.
World & Quests: A large open map (see World Map diagram below) connects varied zones: the Starting Village (tutorial area), Cursed Forests (moonlit wood with fog), Snowy Mountain Pass (Beast trainer), Butterfly Mansion (advanced training/Full Concentration skill), Swordsmith Village/Forge, Haunted Roads (night raids), Spider Mountain Caves (elite slayer boss), and an Endgame Fortress (final raids). Day/night cycles and weather (fog, rain, moonlight) dynamically affect visibility and demon behavior. NPCs follow schedules (working/closing shops in day, hiding at night), and random events (e.g. demon attacks on a caravan, lost child rescues, or chance boss spawns) create a living world. Quests include daily hunts, escort/defense missions, boss investigations, and special trials. Party missions auto-scale: more players = tougher enemies and better rewards.
Building & Tech: The design is modular for Roblox Build. We define core modules (Combat, Movement, UI, etc.) and RemoteEvents for communication. Development is phased: 1) Foundation: world base, controls, spawn points, character/family selection, tutorial obby. 2) Core Combat: weapon equip, attacks, block, dodge, enemy AI, stamina. 3) Progression & Quests: skill tree, breathing trainers, basic quests, party system. 4) World Expansion: add villages, NPCs, day/night, weather, merchant, Butterfly Mansion. 5) Endgame: boss fights (Lower/Upper Moons, Hashira mentors), transformation routes, secret rewards. 6) Polish: UI/UX, effects, sound/music, performance tweaks (especially mobile).

Below are detailed system designs, tables and diagrams to fully specify each element, so that a Roblox Build AI can be instructed to generate the game coherently. Citations reference real Demonfall community knowledge and lore to ground the design in player expectations.

World Layout and Progression
The world is a connected open map with natural transitions. Players first train in the Starting Village (Earth Biome), then venture into increasingly dangerous zones. A sample progression path is:

Breathing Styles & Unlocks
The Slayer path centers on learning Breathing Styles. We classify them by difficulty tier:

Beginner Tier (easy unlock): Water, Flame, Thunder, Beast.
Mid Tier: Wind, Mist, Stone, Love, Serpent, Sound.
Advanced Tier: Insect, Moon, Secret Sun (requires special conditions), future Hybrids.
Each style has a trainer NPC and specific unlock requirements (level, currency, mission). For example, Beast Breathing (Inosuke's style) in Demonfall requires: Level ≥10, 10,000 Yen, Dual Nichirin Swords (obtained from the forge), and speaking to the Beast Trainer in a hidden mountain cave. The trainer's location can require a small navigation or parkour challenge, fitting the lore (e.g. "in a remote cave obscured by bushes"). Once requirements are met, the player pays a fee or completes a mini-quest (e.g. defeating wild beasts), then learns the new style.

Demon Path and Transformations
If the player's prologue "boss" demon wins, the player becomes a Demon. Demons have: auto HP regen, extra mobility, and unique Blood Arts (special skills). The demon progression ladder is:

Minor Demons (random spawns, weaker).
Demon Ranks 1-10 (named demonic fighters).
Lower Moon Bosses 6-1.
Upper Moon Bosses 5-1 (team raids).
Muzan (Ultimate Demon Lord) optional endgame fight.
Players can switch sides mid-game:

A Slayer → Demon requires Muzan's Blood (quest reward or rare merchant item) and a timed "corruption" (24 real-hours that can speed up with level). High-level Slayers (w/ breathing) become a Hybrid demon (Sun-breathing enabled, lore nod to Kokushibo/Kyogai).
A Demon → Slayer can happen via a Wipe Potion (sold by a rare NPC for high cost, or via achievement/quest), which resets your demon state and lets you join the Corps. Demons get exclusive quests (hunt high-value humans, ambush missions) and rewards (demon points, Blood Demon Art unlocks).
Death in normal play is lenient: players simply respawn at their chosen village spawn point with slight penalties (lost time only). Only the introductory fight converts the character.

Quest and Mission System
Missions are accepted from quest boards or NPCs in villages. They auto-complete for party members. Major mission types:

Hunt Missions: Kill X demons in region.
Defense Missions: Defend an NPC/building from waves.
Escort Missions: Protect a villager or merchant.
Investigation Missions: Solve a mystery (find missing person, track demon tracks).
Boss Missions: Unlock and fight a specific Lower/Upper Moon boss (requires group).
Survival Missions: Survive a time period on Demon-infested road.
Dungeon Raids: Clear an enemy camp/cave for loot.
A mission UI lets players select, track progress, and see rewards (currency, XP, skill points, special items).

Boss Ladder
Design bosses in tiers, reflecting Demonfall's Lower/Upper Moons. At least include Lower Moon 6→1, Upper Moon 5→1, plus optional Hashira rivals. Each boss has unique mechanics (e.g. blind spots, minion adds, stage phases). Key bosses: Spider Demon (Lower 6), Bountiful Demon (multi-boss Lower 5), (Lower 1-3 as in series), then Upper Moons like Nakime (teleport map), Gyokko (water demon), Kokushibo (endgame hybrid boss), Muzan (final final). Defeating each yields rare drops (unique abilities or crafting mats).

UI Design
A mobile-first UI with a mirrored PC layout:

Main Screen (HUD): Top corners: minimap (with quest markers). Bottom left: movement joystick (mobile), invisible on PC. Bottom right: four large buttons (Light Attack, Heavy Attack, Dodge/Dash, Block). A Breathing/Buff meter (like "Ki bar") floats near ability buttons. UI should be legible for one-thumb play.

Controls Overlay: Before drawing katana, show an overlay image describing control scheme (mobile and PC). Example labels in Russian: "Нажмите ✤ для лёгкой атаки, □ для блока". Once dismissed, player gets the katana.

Character Creation Screen: Input name, select family (show family banners with buff icons, e.g. +15% DMG). Show preview of avatar. Simple mobile navigation (arrows or swipe).

Spawn/Revival Screen: Let player set their spawn village (applied each death).

Skill Tree UI: Grid with nodes (Breath styles, Strength, Stamina, special moves). Tapping a node shows name, description, cost in points. Branching tree lines. Accessible via menu.

Breathing Styles Screen: List unlocked styles and locked ones (with "How to unlock" tips).

Quest Log: Scrollable list of active/available quests, with objectives and map markers.

Map: Full-screen regional map with icons (towns, trainers, quest locations, bosses). Zoomable on PC, pinch on mobile.

Inventory: Item slots, currency, equip weapon/amulets. Consumables (potions) quick-access.

Party Panel: Shows party members (health bars, revive option). Button to invite/join party.

Settings: Includes Mobile Control Editor: allow players to reposition on-screen buttons. PC controls listed as reference.

prompt:
Create a faithful modern clone of Dolphin Olympics 2 that captures the same flow, momentum, and "one more run" feeling. This is not a realistic dolphin simulator-it is an arcade physics game where the entire experience revolves around building and preserving speed through skillful movement.

The game should use simple controls:
- Hold Up rotates the dolphin's nose upward.
- Hold Down rotates the dolphin's nose downward.
- Rotation is continuous with no angle limits. The player should be able to rotate tail-to-nose in either direction, perform full flips, reverse direction at any time, and chain multiple rotations while airborne.

The dolphin should remain roughly centered on screen at all times. The camera should smoothly follow with spring interpolation and subtle look-ahead based on velocity, revealing more space in the direction of travel without ever feeling like it's chasing the player or snapping. The horizon should remain stable and the camera should never zoom or shake.

Momentum is the core mechanic. Every action should either build speed, preserve speed, or lose speed. Skilled players should be able to continuously generate more momentum through precise timing rather than relying on boost buttons or power-ups.

Water should feel elastic rather than realistic. Perfect entries should preserve momentum and convert it into even greater speed, while poor entries should create drag, large splashes, and significant speed loss. The water surface should act almost like a trampoline that rewards rhythm and precision.

Swimming should be driven entirely by physics and body orientation. There is no swim button. Pointing downward allows the dolphin to accelerate through the water while pointing upward redirects momentum into launches. The player should naturally carve smooth arcs through the water.

The dolphin must be able to grind along the water surface, one of the signature mechanics of Dolphin Olympics 2. At sufficient speed, a shallow angle should allow the dolphin to hydroplane across the surface rather than immediately entering or leaving the water. While grinding, the dolphin should lightly bounce against the surface with subtle springiness, producing white spray and foam while maintaining speed. Grinding should allow players to adjust their angle and set up massive launches. Entering too steeply should force the dolphin underwater, while too shallow an angle should lift it into the air. Grinding should naturally fail if the player loses too much speed.

Jump quality should depend entirely on player skill. Speed, entry angle, exit angle, and timing should determine how high and fast the dolphin launches. Perfect launches should feel explosive while still remaining fully physics-driven.

Airborne movement should feel graceful and weightless without sacrificing momentum. Gravity should be slightly weaker than Earth, allowing long floating arcs. Players should be able to complete multiple flips and smoothly adjust their orientation throughout the jump before re-entering the water.

As speed increases, the game should communicate it visually and audibly. Water spray becomes narrower and longer, foam trails extend, wind noise increases, water entry sounds become more powerful, and dolphin animations become more exaggerated. The camera should subtly anticipate faster movement while always keeping the dolphin comfortably visible.

The dolphin should always feel alive. Even while airborne it should continue subtle tail movement, body flexing, and anticipation poses rather than appearing rigid.

The world consists of an endless stylized ocean with gentle rolling waves under a bright colorful sky. Visuals should be clean, colorful, and readable rather than realistic. The ocean surface should always be easy to judge for timing launches and grinds.

Scoring should reward maximum altitude, longest airtime, highest speed, longest grind distance, flips performed, and maintaining long momentum combos. The combo system should reward alternating smoothly between underwater swimming, surface grinding, and aerial movement without unnecessary interruptions.

Above all, the game should recreate the satisfying flow state of Dolphin Olympics 2. Players should constantly feel that every mistake was understandable, every success was earned through skill, and every run has the potential to go even higher if they execute just a little better.
enriched: Build a 3D endless ocean environment for an arcade-style dolphin movement game focused on flow and momentum. The scene features a wide, gently rolling stylized ocean surface stretching into the horizon under a bright, colorful sky. The water surface is smooth and elastic, designed to visually communicate timing for launches, grinds, and entries with clear, readable waves and subtle foam and spray effects. The dolphin remains roughly centered on screen, with a camera that smoothly follows using spring interpolation and subtle velocity-based look-ahead, keeping the horizon stable and never zooming or shaking. The play space emphasizes open water with no obstacles, allowing the dolphin to carve smooth arcs through the water, grind along the surface with light bouncing and spray, and launch into graceful, weightless aerial arcs with multiple flips. Visual effects intensify with speed, including longer foam trails, narrower spray, and dynamic dolphin animations that convey life and fluid motion. The layout supports continuous momentum-building movement, rewarding skillful transitions between underwater swimming, surface grinding, and airborne maneuvers in a seamless, flowing environment.
